toolkit.heading: What you need to build a website with AI
toolkit.intro: Install the first two before you start. The other two keep your work safe and put it online — free plans are plenty for a small site.

tools.name: Node.js
tools.what: Runs kiss and builds your site. Version 22.12 or later — the LTS download is fine.

tools.name: Claude Code or Codex
tools.what: The coding agent that writes the site for you: Anthropic's Claude Code or OpenAI's Codex. Either works with kiss's skills, and each needs its own account — a Claude account for Claude Code, a ChatGPT account for Codex.

tools.name: Git
tools.what: Keeps every version of your site, so any change can be undone. Push it to GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket to keep a copy online — the hosts below publish straight from GitHub, and most from GitLab or Bitbucket too.

tools.name: A host
tools.what: Puts the finished site on the web. Each builds it from your repository with npm run build and publishes the public folder; each link is that host's own guide to doing it.

setup.heading: From nothing to a live website in six commands
setup.intro: With Node.js and Claude Code or Codex installed, these do the rest.

steps.title: Set it up, in a new folder
steps.text: init installs kiss-ssg, adds a starter site and the build scripts, and points your agent at the API contract. For Claude Code and Codex, the three plugin lines install kiss's skills and the last line opens your agent. Pick the agent you use.

boxes.label: Claude Code
boxes.code:
mkdir my-site && cd my-site
npx kiss-ssg@latest init
claude plugin marketplace add cprobert/kiss-ssg --scope project
claude plugin install kiss-ssg@kiss-ssg --scope project
claude plugin install kiss-memory@kiss-ssg --scope project
claude
boxes.note: The plugins install for this folder. init declares them in the site's settings, but a declared plugin is not installed until these lines run.

boxes.label: Codex
boxes.code:
mkdir my-site && cd my-site
npx kiss-ssg@latest init
codex plugin marketplace add cprobert/kiss-ssg
codex plugin add kiss-ssg@kiss-ssg
codex plugin add kiss-memory@kiss-ssg
codex
boxes.note: init enables the plugins for this folder in .codex/config.toml, but Codex installs them once, for your user, and that also switches them on in every folder: your next site needs only the first two lines and codex.

boxes.label: Other agent
boxes.code:
mkdir my-site && cd my-site
npx kiss-ssg@latest init
boxes.note: For Cursor, Copilot and any other agent: there are no kiss plugins to install, so the skill names in the prompts below mean nothing to it — leave them out. init writes AGENTS.md, which points your agent at node_modules/kiss-ssg/llms.txt; if yours does not read AGENTS.md, ask it to read that file first. Then open your agent in this folder, describe the site, and have it run npm run check.

steps.title: Say what you want
steps.text: In your agent, paste one of these.

prompts.label: A new site
prompts.note: Change the business, the host and the address: kiss writes the sitemap, the feed and every canonical link from them.
prompts.text: Use the kiss-site-new skill to build me a site for a small bakery in Leeds: home, menu, about, and a news section for seasonal specials. It will be served by Netlify at https://kirkgate-bakery.co.uk. Run the build check when you're done.

prompts.label: A site you made in Claude or ChatGPT
prompts.note: kiss is its upgrade path. Paste the link to the published artifact or share in place of the one below — or, if you have it as an HTML file, put it in the folder and name the file instead.
prompts.text: Use the kiss-site-import skill to turn https://claude.ai/public/artifacts/… into a real site, keeping exactly how it looks. Run the build check when you're done.

steps.title: See it, and check it
steps.text: npm run dev serves the site with live reload at the address it prints (localhost:3001 by default) and keeps running — Ctrl-C to stop. npm run check reports every page, broken link and missing launch detail, and publishes nothing: exit 0 means it's right. npm run build writes the site to public/ to deploy.
steps.code:
npm run dev
npm run check

reasons.title: Conventions, not questions
reasons.text: Folders, routes, helpers and asset names all have defaults, so an agent has fewer choices to get wrong, and every default can be overridden.

reasons.title: A verdict, not a log
reasons.text: A failed page or a link to a page that doesn't exist fails the build. Mistakes can't ship quietly.

reasons.title: Readable by the next person
reasons.text: Handlebars views, JSON models and small controllers. Whoever opens the site in two years can follow what the agent wrote.

reasons.title: A memory of the site
reasons.text: npx kiss-ssg aikb records what the site is, so the next session starts from facts rather than guesses.
